newsitem.title: CHINA: China calls for better safety after twin tragedies.
newsitem.headline: China calls for better safety after twin tragedies.

text.p: Chinese leaders called on Sunday for better transportation safety and stricter investigations into accidents after a recent plane crash and rail disaster that together killed at least 135 people.

China should immediately launch a nation-wide inspection into accident-prone industries such as transportation, the Xinhua news agency quoted Vice Premier Wu Bangguo as telling a national video and telephone conference.
Minister of Labour Li Boyong had briefed the conference on two recent major transportation disasters, Xinhua said without elaborating.

At least 35 people were killed when a China Southern Airlines Boeing 737 crash landed at an airport in the southern city of Shenzhen last Thursday in China's worst aviation disaster in nearly three years.
In late April, an estimated 100 people were killed in a train crash in the central province of Hunan, one of the deadliest rail accidents in China for years.
Xinhua did not say if the conference discussed the tragedies, but said Wu had called for tougher measures in handling those guilty of causing mishaps.
"Those leaders and cadres who cause major accidents through bureaucracy or dereliction of duty will be strictly punished," Wu said.
"We will resolutely stop production in those enterprises that harbour hidden dangers, and will resolutely shut down those that should be shut down," Wu said.
The investigation would not be limited to the transportation sector but would include other disaster-prone industries such as mining, construction, power and chemicals, Wu said.
Mining accidents killed nearly 10,000 people in 1996, official figures show.
China has suffered a string of building collapses in recent months, with the last reported disaster killing about 20 people in southern Fujian province in March.
